notes.flakiness_of_rewritten_refusal_tests: The rewritten tests are in-process and deterministic: validate.rs::refusals, check.rs::refusals and response_shape, and the llm.rs refusal tests. They have no sleeps, spawns, sockets, env mutation, fixed paths, shared statics, or unbounded waits. Ordering is stable because the cases are fixed arrays over BTreeMap and BTreeSet. I found no intermittent-failure mechanism.
notes.regression_check_lost_validation: No refusal that a canonical payload can still trigger has been lost. I checked the PayloadBundle and CanonicalJudgePayload code, because I could not diff against the old commit. (1) Zero questions is refused in sc-jev check.rs::prepare and in sc-jev-backends validate.rs::validate_questions, and both are tested. (2) A question with fewer than two distinct choices is refused. Choices are collected into a BTreeSet, so [a, a] is refused too. Both cases are tested in both crates. (3) A duplicate question id is refused by PayloadBundle::encode. (4) The question 'type' check is unreachable. Question has deny_unknown_fields and no type field, so a payload with a type key fails to deserialize. llm.rs::test_unknown_question_type_has_no_answer_schema asserts this. (5) A missing 'prompt' is unreachable. prompt is a required String in Question. A missing system prompt (None) is still refused with INPUT_INVALID, as asserted in llm.rs::test_llm_input_is_refused_like_jev_and_nothing_is_sent. (6) The byte caps (INPUT_TOO_LARGE) and the token cap are still enforced and tested. (7) The reply-side checks all remain against the typed maps: answer-id set, choice membership, exact probability keys, numeric confidence and probability, the model key, and object shape. They are tested in check.rs::parse_outcome_refuses_every_malformed_answer and llm.rs::test_llm_bad_reply_is_typed. One thing I could not confirm is whether the old code refused an empty-string prompt. Neither the sprint doc's dropped-check list nor the assignment mentions one.
